title: Reserved strokes
goal: Know what is pinned before any word is placed, so you know why no word ever takes a punctuation, command or letter stroke.

blocks.x: Every command, punctuation mark and fingerspelled letter in a real keymux config for lyk is pinned **before any word is placed**, ahead of even briefs. A word can never silently take over a stroke such as [[TP-BG]] (`!`).

head: File in `rules/reserved/`
Deployed as
Holds
Where it is listed
rows: 70 strokes: cursor, editing, shortcuts, case and spacing commands, F-keys, Plover control
200 strokes: marks, symbols, and the 52 glued fingerspelling letters
5,475 modifier chords: Ctrl/Alt/Super/Shift plus a letter, digit, symbol or key

items: Nothing generated competes with a reserved stroke: not a word's plain outline, not a brief, not a star form, not an alternate pronunciation, not a phrase, not a backup.

A word that wanted a reserved stroke moves to its next-cheapest outline. Examples: [[captain|KAPT]] would have been `K*P` (the glued capital K), and [[eh|A*EU]] would have been `*E` (the glued letter e).

A reserved stroke can be given back to words only by removing it from the reserved file. [[up|-P]] and [[am|-PL]] sit on `-P` and `-PL` for that reason: the period has 30 other strokes and does not need them.

blocks.x: The build refuses to run if a brief named `[word]` in `rules/briefs.toml` has a literal outline that is reserved. Before that check, `up` silently lost `-P` and fell back to the two-key `UP`.
The lists themselves are on the next pages: [punctuation and commands](#/ref/punctuation), [fingerspelling, numbers and modifiers](#/ref/fingerspelling).
